judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deems the Owner subject to Contractor-like obligations when self-performing; the cross-references are specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.1.1 and 6.2; no separate contracts are identified here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable opportunity' for introduction and storage is soft but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits 6.1.3 coordination and 3.13.1 use of site.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Failure to report is deemed an acknowledgment that other construction is fit, 'except as to defects not then reasonably discoverable'—a deeming rule with a discoverability escape that invites argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels 3.2.1's review duties and 4.3.4's concealed-conditions right without direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allocates costs of 'improperly timed activities, damage to the Work or defective construction' both ways; the categories are stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reads with 4.3.6 claim grounds and Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1's Change Order requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Damage wrongfully caused' imports a fault standard that the clause does not define.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-refers to 10.2.5, which uses a different (causation-and-responsibility) formula; the two sit together loosely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line equivalence rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.14 and 6.1.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dispute-triggered self-help and cost-allocation rule; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.15 and 7.5.3's reimbursement of debris removal.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Lists the three instruments by which changes may be made, 'subject to the limitations stated in this Article 7 and elsewhere in the Contract Documents.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 narrows this to Change Orders except under 7.3 and 9.7.1, and Addendum 6.5 adds a fast-track Change Order procedure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise definition requiring preparation by the Architect and signature by Owner, Contractor and Architect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 makes the Change Order the sole route to a Contract Sum change while Addendum 6.5 contemplates Change Orders issued as items are priced; the signature formalities are not repeated there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fragmentary cross-reference to the permitted methods of adjustment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 6.1-6.3 override the meaning of 'cost' and 'fee' in these methods, which is an express reconciliation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition and the Owner's unilateral directive power are stated, though the transcription is fragmentary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 preserves Paragraph 7.3 as an exception, so directives remain available; Agreement 6.1 governs the resulting adjustment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four alternative methods including 'cost to be determined in a manner agreed upon by the parties and a mutually acceptable fixed or percentage fee'—an agreement-to-agree limb.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 6.1-6.3 redefine 'cost' as the Cost of the Work and 'fee' as the Contractor's Fee, and the fee here is a lump sum, so applying these methods requires reading three provisions together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A duty to proceed promptly with a directed change; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.3.3 and Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1's carve-out for 7.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Signature converts a directive into a recorded Change Order; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 7.2.1 and 7.3.9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Actual net cost as confirmed by the Architect' and the netting rule for combined additions and credits are workable but fiddly in application.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 6.2-6.3 substitute the Contractor's Fee for 'overhead and profit,' and the Fee is a lump sum that deletions do not obviously reduce; 6.4 provides only equitable adjustment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The interim-determination mechanism is dense and the transcription is poor, but the structure (interim certification, later Change Order, right to claim) is stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.1.7.1 expressly incorporates this subparagraph for amounts not in dispute; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Agreement is effective immediately and recorded by Change Order; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.2.3 makes each Change Order a final settlement, which builds on this without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Minor changes ... not involving adjustment in the Contract Sum or extension of the Contract Time and not inconsistent with the intent of the Contract Documents' packs three qualifiers into one authority.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(c) requires Owner and Architect approval of field-condition minor changes and 1.1.2.1 adds Owner concurrence generally, so the Architect's unilateral authority here is curtailed elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines Contract Time as a period allotted for Substantial Completion; clear as a definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Revised 4.3 states a calendar completion date rather than a period, and 4.2 measures time from a commencement date that revised 4.1 makes permit-contingent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line definition referring to the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement's 4.1 says 'approximately the Fifteenth of July' and the Addendum makes it 'pending approval of permits,' so the Agreement does not establish the firm date this definition assumes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ties the date to the Architect's certification under 9.8; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 4.4 pays a bonus if the work 'is determined to be substantially complete' without naming the decider, and Addendum 12.2.1 introduces a recorded Notice of Completion as a further milestone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional default to calendar days.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the various day-counts in the Agreement and Supplementary Conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Time limits stated in the Contract Documents are of the essence' is emphatic and clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No liquidated damages were inserted at 4.3, the only time incentive is the indefinite 4.4 bonus, and 4.1 makes commencement permit-contingent—so what time-is-of-the-essence secures is unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three distinct rules (no premature operations, commencement date unaffected by insurance, five days' notice for filings) are packed into one paragraph but each is stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 4.1 leaves blank the Owner's time requirement for filing mortgages and mechanic's liens, which is exactly what this notice provision serves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Expeditiously with adequate forces' is a qualitative performance standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reads with 8.2.1 and Addendum Article 2's staffing requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of delay causes ending in 'other causes beyond the Contractor's control' and 'other causes which the Architect determines may justify delay'—an open catch-all after enumerated specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 4.3.7.4 bars separate increases for concurrent or interrelated delays and 7.1.3.1 requires a Change Order, so entitlement to extension is governed by three provisions with different emphases.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.3.7 and Supplementary Conditions 4.3.7.3-4.3.7.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence asserts that the Contract Sum 'is stated in the Agreement' and is the total amount payable—an assertion of fact about another document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement states no sum: 5.1.1 defines the Contract Sum as Cost of the Work plus Fee and 5.2.1's guaranteed maximum is 'N/A,' so the definition on which 9.5.1, 9.6.7, 11.4.1 and 14.2.4 depend has no figure behind it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At least ten days before the date established for each progress payment' and 'notarized, if required' are clear, if conditional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.1.2-12.1.3 set their own application and payment dates with the numerals left blank, and retainage 'as provided in the Contract Documents' is stated as 'N/A' in 12.1.7.3 and five percent in the Addendum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive inclusion rule cross-referring to 7.3.8.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 limits Contract Sum changes to Change Orders except under 7.3, which preserves this route.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditions for paying for stored materials are spelled out, including title protection and insurance costs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.5.6 and 12.1.7.2 impose parallel Owner-approval conditions; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The title warranty is qualified 'to the best of the Contractor's knowledge, information and belief,' which softens an otherwise absolute promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 12.1.4(b) requires lien waivers above $2,500 and revised 12.2.2 a lien-free title endorsement, layering evidence requirements on top of this warranty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A seven-day certification deadline with two stated alternatives; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.3 states that its time periods 'supersede those stated in Subparagraph 9.4.1,' so this deadline is expressly displaced for final certification and left in place for progress payments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long, heavily qualified description of what a Certificate does and does not represent; carefully drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.1.9 adds a parallel disclaimer of detailed examination and puts verification with the Owner's accountants; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Grounds .4 ('reasonable evidence that the Work cannot be completed for the unpaid balance of the Contract Sum') and .6 (unpaid balance inadequate for 'actual or liquidated damages') presuppose a fixed sum and a damages clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: There is no stated Contract Sum or Guaranteed Maximum Price (5.1.1, 5.2.1) and no liquidated damages provision at 4.3, so two of the seven enumerated withholding grounds cannot be applied as written.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line release rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.5.1 and 12.1.7.6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Payment 'in the manner and within the time provided in the Contract Documents'—an entirely referential obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The referenced timing is in Agreement 12.1.3, whose day numerals are blank or illegible, and in the revised 12.2.2 for final payment; the obligation is only as definite as those.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Prompt payment to subcontractors 'reflecting percentages actually retained' is clear in principle.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Retainage in this contract is stated three ways—'N/A' in the printed 12.1.7.3, five percent in the Addendum, and not less than ten percent for subcontractors in 12.1.8—so what percentage is 'actually retained' is uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short disclaimer with a saving clause for legal requirements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 9.6.2.1 allows the Owner to make joint payments while disclaiming any obligation to subcontractors, which is consistent with this.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An equivalence rule for material suppliers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.6.2 and Supplementary Condition 9.6.2.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short non-acceptance rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.9.3 and 12.3.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It creates a holding obligation and then disclaims fiduciary liability, tort liability, segregation and punitive damages—an obligation stripped of most remedies, keyed to 'the full penal sum of the Contract Sum.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No Contract Sum is stated (5.1.1, 5.2.1) and Article 16 requires no payment bond, so the trigger for the holding obligation cannot be measured.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The stop-work right and its consequences are specific, subject to the seven-day and seven-day windows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs from 'the date established in the Contract Documents,' which Agreement 12.1.3 leaves blank, and adds 'interest as provided for in the Contract Documents,' which 14.2 states as 'N/A.'

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sufficiently complete ... so that the Owner can occupy or utilize the Work for its intended use' is the most litigated standard in the form, especially where completion dates and bonuses depend on it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Revised 4.3 fixes a completion date, 4.4 pays a bonus for early substantial completion without saying who determines it, and Addendum 12.2.1 adds a recorded Notice of Completion—three milestones keyed to this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Comprehensive list of items to be completed or corrected' with an express non-waiver; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.8.3-9.8.5 and Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The inspection standard mirrors 9.8.1's 'intended use' test; the procedure is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 adds Owner concurrence to Architect determinations, which affects this inspection.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Certificate establishes date, responsibilities and warranty commencement 'unless otherwise provided in the Certificate,' which leaves the content partly to the Architect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 12.2.2.1's one-year correction period runs from Substantial Completion and Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 controls warranty delivery, so the warranty timeline depends on several texts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Payment of retainage on acceptance and surety consent; the mechanism is stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The retainage percentage is stated inconsistently ('N/A' in the printed 12.1.7.3, five percent in the Addendum, ten percent for subcontractors in 12.1.8), so the amount to be released is unsettled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A joint-inspection requirement; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.9.1 and 11.4.1.5's insurer consent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short non-acceptance rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.6.6 and 12.3.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final-certificate conditions and representations are detailed and internally consistent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.3 substitutes an accountant-driven basis and timetable for final certification, and Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 forbids issuance until the Owner accepts all warranties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Five enumerated submittals with a bond alternative for refused waivers; specific, though 'other data ... in such form as may be designated by the Owner' is open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 12.1.4(b) already requires progress lien waivers and revised 12.2.2 requires a lien-free title endorsement, so the lien-clearing obligations are cumulative across three provisions.
